name: dc-motor-drv8833
title: DC motor driver DRV8833: two motors (or one stepper) with its VM, VCP and VINT capacitors
about: A TI DRV8833 (HTSSOP-16 with PowerPAD) drives two brushed DC motors from VM 2.7–10.8 V, up to 1.5 A RMS and 2 A peak per bridge (datasheet SLVSAR1E at VM 5 V, 25 °C), each on a JST XH connector. As the datasheet asks: a 10 µF-class ceramic at VM, 10 nF from VCP to VM, 2.2 µF at VINT; a 100 µF electrolytic as the motor supply's local bulk capacitor. A 10 kΩ pull-down holds nSLEEP low – bridges off, inputs ignored – until the firmware drives it high; nFAULT has its pull-up. The bridge outputs clamp the windings with their own body diodes (clamp internal): no flyback diodes. Sense pins to ground: no current chopping, the overcurrent protection stays.

ports.vm: the motor supply, 2.7–10.8 V (11.8 V absolute maximum)
ports.vcc: the logic supply of the MCU (3.3 V or 5 V) – nFAULT's pull-up
ports.sleep: nSLEEP from an MCU output: high = run, low = sleep (bridges off)
ports.fault: nFAULT to an MCU input: low on overcurrent, overtemperature or undervoltage

components.label: {as}: dual H-bridge DRV8833
components.notes: PowerPAD (pin 17) and GND (13) to ground; thermal vias from the pad to a ground plane (datasheet 10.1.1).

components.label: {as}: VM ceramic 22 µF
components.notes: Datasheet (pin functions, 10.1): a low-ESR ceramic of 10 µF minimum, rated for VM, close to the VM pin. 22 µF because an X5R keeps only part of its value under DC bias; 25 V for VM up to 10.8 V (edakit's margin × 1.5: 16.2 V).

components.label: {as}: VM bulk 100 µF electrolytic
components.notes: Local bulk capacitance (datasheet 9.1: the size is left to system-level testing; figure 7 shows a polarized 10 µF at VM). 100 µF is a design choice for the start and stall pulses of small motors; 25 V above VM, as 9.1 asks for the energy a motor returns.

components.label: {as}: charge pump 10 nF VCP to VM
components.notes: Datasheet (pin functions, 10.1): 0.01 µF X7R rated 16 V minimum from VCP to VM, not to ground; this one 50 V.

components.label: {as}: VINT 2.2 µF
components.notes: Datasheet (pin functions, 10.1): 2.2 µF ceramic rated 6.3 V from VINT to ground; this one 16 V.

components.label: {as}: nSLEEP pull-down 10 k
components.notes: Holds nSLEEP low while the MCU pin floats (reset, boot): bridges off, charge pump stopped, inputs ignored (datasheet 7.3.4). Firmer than the internal 500 kΩ; an output at 3.3 V drives 0.33 mA into it.

components.label: {as}: nFAULT pull-up 10 k
components.notes: nFAULT is open drain, VOL ≤ 0.5 V at 5 mA (datasheet 6.5); 10 kΩ from 3.3 V or 5 V draws well below that.

components.label: {as}: motor A (JST XH, 1 = AOUT1)
components.notes: JST XH, 3 A with AWG 22 wire: above the bridge's 2 A peak. Another family than the JST PH supply input (block power-input-jst), so that a supply plug does not fit.

nets.name: vcp
nets.notes: Charge pump above VM; the datasheet gives no VCP voltage – 10.8 V (VM max) + 6.3 V (the rating asked of the VINT capacitor) as an assumed upper bound.

nets.name: vint
nets.notes: Internal supply; the datasheet gives no voltage – 6.3 V, the rating it asks of the VINT capacitor, as the upper bound.

notes: VM 2.7–10.8 V (recommended operating conditions; 11.8 V absolute maximum – a full 3-cell LiPo is above it). The motor supply needs no reverse-polarity diode in series: behind one the energy a braking motor returns lifts VM (HINT.motor_supply); protect the input with a P-MOSFET (block reverse-pmos) or a clamp behind the diode.

Bridge logic (datasheet table 1): xIN1 = xIN2 = 0 coast (outputs Z), 1/0 forward, 0/1 reverse, 1/1 brake. PWM on one input with the other low = fast decay, with the other high = slow decay (table 2). VIH 2 V, VIL 0.7 V, inputs up to 5.75 V: 3.3 V and 5 V logic drive them; nSLEEP needs 2.5 V. Up to 1 ms after nSLEEP goes high before the bridges switch (tWAKE).

While the firmware starts: R1 keeps the driver asleep, and the bridge inputs have internal 150 kΩ pull-downs (coast). Where the firmware never needs sleep, nSLEEP may go to VM through 20–75 kΩ instead of R1 and the MCU pin (datasheet 7.3.4: the pin clamps at 6.5 V, at most 250 µA into it).

AISEN and BISEN go to ground: no current chopping (7.3.3). To limit start and stall current, a sense resistor per bridge, R = 0.2 V / ICHOP (VTRIP 160–240 mV), rated for I²R. The overcurrent protection (IOCP 2–3.3 A, retry after 1.35 ms) works without them.

The outputs carry clamp internal – the body diodes take the winding current in fast decay (7.3.2): REQ.missing asks for no flyback diode, and a single diode across a winding driven both ways would short the bridge.

edakit check warns LVL.undefined/open_drain on the motor nets (the outputs are tristate): Z in coast or sleep, where the motor is meant to run free – a bridge output, no logic line. HINT.motor_supply appears once a motor (kind motor) is in the graph.

Unused inputs to ground (coast) – edakit wants two pins on every net (STRUCT.net), as the block's test does with AIN2, BIN1 and BIN2. The two bridges may be paralleled for one motor of up to 3 A RMS (datasheet 8.2, figure 7): AIN1 with BIN1, AIN2 with BIN2, AOUT1 with BOUT1, AOUT2 with BOUT2.

sim.json: the driving nets under the MCU's outputs. The DRV8833 has no behaviour model (behavior none) – edakit sim checks the nets, the pull resistors and the capacitors' voltages, not the motor current: the stall current V / R_winding against the overcurrent trip, the 3 A of the connectors and the bulk capacitor's ripple rating (93 mA rms at 120 Hz; the ceramic C1 is meant to carry the PWM ripple) are the review's.

t_run.about: the driver awake (nSLEEP high), bridge A forward
